title: Interpreting jurisdictional and procedural statutes
summary: Statutory interpretation determines the reach of the enacted words that authorize and limit judicial action. The assigned cases use text, structure, history, and institutional consequences while disagreeing about their weight.
notes: A later statutory amendment may change the rule examined in an older case.

sections.Meaning: Statutory interpretation determines the reach of the enacted words that authorize and limit judicial action. The assigned cases use text, structure, history, and institutional consequences while disagreeing about their weight.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the statutory language at the time of the decision, the question it answers, and the competing readings. Exxon, Home Depot, and the venue cases show why ordinary intuitions about convenient litigation cannot replace the enacted conditions.
